scope: Additive public-evidence recheck for the permanent Furnace L1-4 and required Firemite L1-4 lifecycle. No inferred schedule or Core behaviour is enabled.
game_version: March 2025 launch evidence and April 2026 official interaction note, consulted on 2026-09-20.

sources.title: Welcome to Clash Anytime Update!
sources.limitations: Confirms an immobile Furnace which releases Firemites that target and burn Buildings. It gives no duration, count, schedule, self-decay, targeting tie-break, coordinates, jump, collision or flame pulse definition.

sources.title: March Update Sneak Peek #2: New Troop, New Equipment and Other Changes!
sources.version: March 2025 sneak peek; game/client build not published
sources.limitations: Reports a 60-second window, approximate one Firemite every three seconds, L1-L4 caps 19/20/21/22, parent self-damage, loss of unspawned children if destroyed, and non-stacking fire pools. Its cadence is explicitly approximate and omits initial delay, exact intervals, decay rate, healing/freezing boundary semantics, target tie-breaks, coordinates, jump/collision and flame geometry/pulses; it cannot define deterministic ticks.

sources.title: THE SOUND OF CLASH UPDATE
sources.limitations: Confirms Siege Machines now take damage from Firemite fires. It does not quantify the fire, identify its centre/radius, define stacking, pulse timing, targets or ordering.

sources.title: Furnace / Firemite
sources.limitations: Searchable public summary corroborates periodic spawns, nearest-building behaviour, a jump, and persistent fire, but direct consultation failed with a server payment-response. No value or rule from it is imported as current deterministic evidence.

published_lifecycle.fire_pool_overlap: same-place pools do not stack damage

non_materializable: The advertised cadence is approximate (about one every three seconds), not a tick-aligned schedule or an initial-spawn delay.
The self-damage amount and exact lifetime/end ordering are absent.
Healing and freezing state boundaries are absent from primary evidence.
Spawn coordinates, Firemite target tie-breaks, jump flight/collision and fire centre, radius, duration, pulse, target eligibility and same-tick ordering remain absent.

known_uncertainties: Dividing 60 seconds by a 19-22 cap would invent an interval and cannot establish an initial delay or final-spawn boundary.
The primary April 2026 note proves that Firemite fire affects Siege Machines but does not supply a reusable persistent-area contract.
No exact source-backed Core, Headless, Viewer, RL, snapshot or replay lifecycle is materialized by this delta.
conclusion: The lifecycle evidence is stronger but still insufficient for deterministic implementation. Furnace and Firemite remain data-only: exact spawn times, parent decay and persistent-fire geometry/timing are necessary before a shared Core actor can be enabled.
